t: Born of the 1830 revolution against the United Kingdom of the Netherlands, it was recognised as neutral by the great powers in 1839.
It was continental Europe’s first industrial nation and, through Leopold II, the ruler of the Congo, where forced labour cost countless lives.
Conflict between Dutch and French speakers turned it into a federal state in 1993, while Brussels became home to the EU and NATO.
dyk: Belgium’s line from Brussels to Mechelen, opened in May 1835, was the first steam passenger railway in continental Europe, built and run by the state itself.
ev: Revolution in Brussels; a provisional government declares independence
Leopold I takes the oath as first King of the Belgians
The Treaty of London recognises Belgium and guarantees its neutrality
The powers recognise Leopold II’s Congo Free State
Germany invades; the Belgian army holds the Yser front until 1918
A constitutional reform makes Belgium a federal state

f.founder: Provisional Government of 1830; Leopold I of Belgium
